ecology.title: The Guardian of the Dry Forest
ecology.subtitle: An ancestral symbiosis etched in scarlet feathers.
ecology.content: The Scarlet Macaw is not just an inhabitant; it is the architect of the canopy. In the rigor of the Guanacaste dry forest, its existence is tied to giants like the Ceiba and the Tempisque. As a seed disperser and occupant of natural cavities, its presence dictates the health and future of local biodiversity.

threats.title: Silent Threats
threats.subtitle: An ecosystem in precarious balance.
threats.content: The fragmentation of the dry forest and illegal nest poaching have pushed the Scarlet Macaw to the brink of the abyss. It is not just about the loss of space; it is the interruption of life cycles spanning decades.
threats.quote: Every fallen tree is one less nest, a generation lost in the forest echo.

recovery.title: The Path of Return
recovery.subtitle: Science and community in action for life.
recovery.content: The recovery of the Scarlet Macaw in Guanacaste is one of the greatest conservation successes in the dry tropics. Through artificial nests and constant monitoring, we have managed to reverse a trend that seemed irreversible.

sightseeing.title: Ethical Sighting
sightseeing.subtitle: Observing without intervening is the greatest act of respect.
sightseeing.content: The Scarlet Macaw is a sensitive species. Your presence must be invisible for their behavior to remain natural. Follow these guidelines to ensure your encounter is positive for both you and the birds.
dos: Maintain a minimum distance of 20 meters.
Wear neutral colors that blend with the forest.
Speak quietly and avoid sudden movements.
donts: Do not feed the birds under any circumstances.
Do not use flashes or intense lights.
Do not play bird call recordings (playback).
Do not attempt to touch or chase individuals.
